name: Flotsam-Glacia
specific_features: Escape pod debris field: three hundred cryo-stasis pods from the prison transport Chains of Solace are scattered across the Sorrow Shelf glacier, most of them shattered or drifted half-buried, each still bearing its prisoner's case number etched in frost.

Automated beacon: one pod, case number 117, sank forty meters into the ice and continues to emit a medical distress ping and a faint heat signature eighty years after the crash—its stasis cell, by every reading, is still cycling.
description: Flotsam-Glacia is a world of white silence, its surface a single ice sheet fractured into pressure ridges and deep crevasse fields that glow teal where crystal caverns open below. The thin atmosphere carries a permanent diamond-dust haze that makes the low sun a smeared halo on the horizon. Frozen methane lakes lie embedded in the shelf like panes of smoked glass.

Cold here is total: exposed metal snaps like dry twigs, breath-ice welds visors shut, and sound travels with a flat cracked quality across the ridges. In the caverns beneath, the dark hums faintly with the magnetic anomaly at the pole, and instruments drift out of true. Travelers report the strange conviction of being followed across the featureless white.

Eighty years ago the prison transport Chains of Solace lost attitude control and scattered three hundred cryo-pods across the Sorrow Shelf before burning up on approach. Most pods were never opened; their occupants remain sealed, names and sentences etched in frost. The wreck's black box recorded a final order from the bridge—jettison all prisoners—that no court ever authorized.

Salvage firms mine dark crystals from the caverns within sight of the debris field, and more than one crew has quietly pried open a pod looking for anything worth selling. Pod 117 still pings from under the ice, its heat signature steady through eight decades, and last year the ping changed to a pattern matching an old naval SOS. Whoever is inside has been awake far longer than the stasis systems should allow.
